- Overweight recent highs in forecasts when sentiment is positive (especially >0.4) — model tends to overreact and overshoot.
- Underweight early drops or mean-reversion signals when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment <0.4) — model fails to adjust downward.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent lag in correcting for recent price dips — model often takes 2–3 days to react to sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is consistently low (0.0–0.2) over 3+ days, model tends to forecast higher prices, creating false “recovery” signals.
- After sharp spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often forecasts continued upward momentum, ignoring mean reversion — especially if sentiment drops post-spike.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 10 days of the 30d horizon — model overestimates volatility early, then undercorrects.
- Sentiment history with multiple 0.0 values (e.g., 3+ consecutive) triggers model to overcorrect — forecast becomes too conservative or too aggressive depending on prior trend.
